(b) Trap 1: High > 0 everywhere, so day_pos_ratio(High) is about 1 across the whole cross-section. After cs_last_low10's ordinal rank it becomes a static ramp in column order. It is then wrapped in a 5-day F-value, a 20-day residual and a 30-day correlation, and it measures nothing readable.

Same column-order ramp cs_last_low10(day_pos_ratio(High), day_at_min_ratio(Vwap)) as regressor (trap 1), other side is F-of-F cross_reg_fvalue(day_mean(Open), cross_reg_fvalue(...), 5); no readable measure (b).

Two 5-day F-values (es_ratio_lo(Vwap) vs argmax(High), mean(Open) vs argmax(High)) -> 20-day ts_regres residual -> 30-day corr with volume^3.75; three stacked rolling-regression statistics on back-adjusted price level, no mechanism (b).

All leaves are back-adjusted price levels (day_quantile_q25(Open), day_close(Open)); y is monotone in price and the nested cs_first_high20 with div(...,-5) just lifts the ~20-40% price-rank band to the top; back-adjusted price is not a real price level (trap 3); train +0.59 vs valid +2.76 jump also not stable-looking (b).

(b) The dependent variable is cs_rank(pow_05(ts_regbeta(...))). Inside it, the cross-sectional mean of back-adjusted Close (a meaningless price level, trap 3) is regressed over 5 days on ts_var(LogFloatCap,20) plus the constant cs_median(day_pos_ratio(Open)), which is always 1. This outer value then gets a 241-day beta against q75 Volume. It is unreadable nesting with no mechanism, so a numbers game.

(a) It has the same skeleton as #2: cross_regbeta(day_quantile_q75(Volume), cs_bucket_demean(add(const, ts_var(LogFloatCap,.)), LimitWidth), 30). Only the variance window changes (20 instead of 30), and the added constant is cancelled by the bucket demean. |rho|=0.63 with #2, so it is a rewrite of #2.

(b) day_zero_ratio(Open) is about 0 for every stock because adjusted Open is always positive. The ordinal rank inside cs_last_low05 turns these ties into a column-order ramp (trap 1). The only real content is pushing the bottom 5% of LogTotalCap down, so direction -1 goes long the smallest 5% of caps (size control skin, trap 2). |rho| is at most 0.08 against everything, which fits a ramp.

(a)(b) The value is dominated by multiplying with the market-cap rank: |rho| is 0.55 with cap, 0.39 with liquidity and 0.37 with the known family. cs_last_low05(LogTotalCap,LogTotalCap) flips the bottom 5% of caps negative, and abs_ flips them back to about 1, which makes a cap sawtooth at 5%. The top 10% of day_corr(Ret,Open) is also replaced by the mean. It is a cap-shape trick, not an intraday-correlation mechanism.

(a) day_zero_ratio(Ret) is the classic zero-return illiquidity measure (|rho| 0.42 with liquidity, 0.38 with the known family), and multiplying by its own rank is only a monotone transform. cs_last_low05(., LogTotalCap) makes the smallest 5% of caps negative, so direction -1 puts them straight into the long book. It is a rewrite of the liquidity and size controls.

(b) Warm-up artifact. cross_ema(A^3, 241) with A = X^3 / sum of X^3 over the last 241 days. A is exactly 1 on each stock's first valid day (x/x), then decays roughly as 1/d. Cubed, those first days are about 1 in size, while genuine volume spikes give A^3 of only 1e-5 to 1e-2, and the 241-day half-life keeps the first days' weight for years. In a synthetic simulation, 94-99% of the value over 4 years came from the first 60 days after the first bar, with rank correlation 0.87-0.98 to that part. So the cross-sectional ranking reflects the date of the stock's first bar (listing age, data start, long suspensions) plus its early volume path, not the intended volume-burstiness mechanism. Its 0.31 correlation with market cap also fits a recent-IPO tilt.

Its band, cross_quantile_q25(signedpower(core of #2), 241), means a stock sat in the late-volume band on most days of the past year. That is #2's day_centroid(Volume) band written another way. Its ordering term takes the square of a lexicographic rank, applies two 241-day quantiles, then a 20-day ts_argmin. It does not read as measuring anything. Its |rho| is only 0.20, but the mechanism is the same, so the 1.73 train Sharpe looks like fitting on top of #2's mechanism.

It then takes a 241-day quantile and a 20-day argmin of that F-value. Pure numbers game.

(b) Nested numeric game. The result passes through pow_05 and cs_rank, then a 241-day cross_regbeta on q75 minute share volume. cs_median(day_pos_ratio(Open)) is about 1 every day, so it is a dead term. No mechanism can be read from it.

(b)/trap 2. The core input ts_var(LogFloatCap,30) is the variance of the market-cap level (volatility plus trend), so it re-skins controls. Its 30-day cross_regbeta on q75 share volume is not scale-free, and across stocks it is driven mainly by the unit ratio std(var)/std(share volume). The constant cs_median(day_pos_ratio(Open)) is dead and is removed exactly by the bucket demean. LimitWidth takes only a few values, and _buckets uses ordinal ranks, so the large tied blocks are split into deciles by column order.

(b)/trap 1. Open is a positive back-adjusted price, so day_zero_ratio(Open) ties at 0 for nearly every stock. The ordinal _pct_rank inside cs_last_low05 then turns that tie block into a static ramp in column order. The only stock-specific content left is the bottom 5% of LogTotalCap, which direction -1 moves into the long book: a size step at the tail (trap 2). Its |rho| is at most 0.08 against every control and every other head, which fits a static ramp.

Trap 2. abs_(top-masked intraday corr(Ret,Open) x LogTotalCap rank) is mainly a market-cap rank: |rho| is 0.55 with market cap, 0.39 with liquidity and 0.37 with the known family. cs_last_low05(LogTotalCap, LogTotalCap) followed by abs_ folds the smallest 5% up to about 0.95-1, a V-shaped kink that a rank-cubic residual cannot remove. Multiplying by an abs'd, top-masked correlation is a numeric game.

Trap 2. day_zero_ratio(Ret) is multiplied by its own rank after cs_last_low05 has pushed the bottom 5% of LogTotalCap down. Every value in that bottom 5% is <=0 and every other value is >=0. Direction -1 therefore puts the smallest 5% of stocks by total cap into the long book as a block, whatever the signal says. That block is about half of the long decile and is a size tail step the rank-cubic residual cannot remove. The other half is picked by the lowest zero-return share, which has |rho| 0.42 with liquidity and 0.38 with the known family.
